data.name: [Path of Crimson] [Part I: The Sunset Road]
data.description:
You step into the Administration Building at Wake Island. The air is heavy with the scent of burning incense, mingling with faint traces of ash. Dusk is waiting by the window, his glowing eyes fixed on the horizon. His golden scarf billows gently, though there’s no wind.

"Ah, there you are. I’ve been waiting. The Sunset Road is burning—quite literally. Caravans have been destroyed, cargo vanished, and the culprits remain in the shadows.”

“This isn’t random. It reeks of the Black Maw. They don’t simply attack—they calculate, they take, and they leave nothing but ash in their wake.”

“I need you to investigate. Follow the trail. Find out what they’re after. And if you run into resistance...”

Dusk smirks, his fiery scarf shifting with the breeze.

“Well, let’s just say they won’t be calculating much after you’re done.”

“Start at the caravan site. You’ll find it near Sector 338. And remember—anything you find may burn, but it won’t destroy the truth.”

data.name: [Path of Crimson] [Part II: The Ember Trail]
data.description:
The sky glows with the colors of twilight as Dusk stands at the edge of Wake Island, his golden scarf flickering in the breeze. His gaze is distant, his expression thoughtful, but when you approach, he turns to you with a faint smirk.

"Ah, there you are. I thought perhaps the embers had swallowed you, but you’re too stubborn for that, aren’t you?"

His smirk fades, and he gestures toward a map spread across a nearby stone. The parchment is old, singed at the edges, with three locations marked: The Flamebinding Altar, Infernal Pool, and Ember Crossroads.

"The Black Maw’s flames burn hotter along the Ember Trail. This isn’t just another raid—they’re targeting sacred sites. These seals aren’t just relics. They’re bindings, meant to hold dangerous energies. If they succeed in breaking them, the fires won’t stop with these sites."

He looks back at you, his tone quieter but heavier with meaning.

"Seals like these don’t just break—they shatter. Shadows twist, fire spreads, and what’s unleashed doesn’t go back easily. You’ll need to stop them. Follow the trail, disrupt their rituals, and bring me anything you find."

He pauses, his fiery scarf shifting slightly, as though caught in an unseen current.

"And be careful. What the Maw touches leaves marks that don’t fade."

As he hands you the map, his eyes meet yours, the intensity behind them unmistakable.

"Go. Fire destroys, but it also reveals. Just don’t let it consume you."

His gaze lingers on the horizon for a moment before he turns back to the village, his scarf glowing faintly in the dimming light.

data.name: [Path of Crimson] [Part III: Chains of Deception]
data.description:
There's something wrong.

The moment you step onto Wake Island, you feel it. The air is heavy, thick with the lingering scent of burned wood, but it’s more than that. It’s the silence. The way the ocean barely stirs against the docks. The way the distant embers on the mainland still glow, flickering like open wounds across the land.

And then there’s Dusk.

He stands where he always does, near the island’s edge, his golden scarf resting against his shoulders instead of shifting with the wind. He doesn’t greet you with his usual smirk. He doesn’t say anything at all—not at first. When he finally does speak, it’s slower. Measured. Less like an old friend and more like someone choosing their words carefully.

“It’s worse than I expected.”

His gaze doesn’t leave the horizon. Even as he gestures toward the burned parchment on the nearby table, his fingers move almost mechanically, without the usual casual confidence.

“The Maw isn’t just raiding anymore. They’re following a pattern. Marking sites. The Ember Trail was only the beginning.”

On the map, two locations are circled in deep red ink. His hand lingers over them for a moment longer than necessary.

“If they finish what they’ve started, we’re out of time. We need to act first.”

And then—finally—he looks at you. But something is missing.

The usual sharp glint in his eyes isn’t there. His expression is neutral, his posture stiff, too still.

For the first time since you met him, Dusk looks like he’s waiting. Not just for your answer, but for your reaction.

“Destroy their operations. Take anything they were using. If they’re preparing something bigger, I want to know what it is.”

His voice is steady, but there’s something beneath it. Not doubt. Not hesitation. Just… calculation.

And then, softer—

“…And don’t hesitate. If you run into resistance, you know what to do.”

That, at least, sounds like him. But somehow, it makes everything else feel even stranger.

He hands you the map, his fingers brushing against yours for just a second longer than they should. It’s barely noticeable. But when he pulls away, he does it just a little too deliberately.

“Go. We don’t have time to waste.”

And with that, he turns back to the horizon, as if dismissing the conversation entirely. But for the first time, you’re not sure if he’s watching the burning sky—

—or making sure you’re leaving.

data.name: A Call for Aid from the Grovetender
data.description:
A Call for Aid from the Grovetender
Something is wrong in the Shining Expanse. The Sandworms, ancient beasts that sleep beneath the dunes, have begun to rampage. They tear through the land without reason, destroying everything in their path.

I am The Grovetender, guardian of this land. I do not know what has disturbed the Sandworms, but their destruction is spreading. Sunny the Tree, the oldest and most sacred tree in the desert, is in danger. If it falls, the balance of life here will be lost, and the village of Shirohana will suffer.

I cannot stop this alone. I call upon the Global Anbu—warriors of skill and courage—to help defend the tree and uncover the cause of this disaster. Time is running out, and the sands do not wait for anyone.

Will you answer?

—Grovetender of Shirohana
data.successDescription: As the waves crash against the shores of Wake Island, the silence feels almost unreal after the chaos of the desert. The battle with the Alpha Sandworm is over, but its memory lingers—each scar, each grain of sand still clinging to your gear, a reminder of what you faced. The Grovetender’s words echo in your mind, a mix of gratitude and warning, knowing the balance of the dunes has shifted.

data.description: The Order launders its blacksteel through the free port at Wake Island. Enter the island's sparring circuit as cover, follow the tide manifests, and earn the case officer's exam recommendation.
data.successDescription: Circuit fought, shipment stopped, Chunin Exams recommendation signed.

objectives.description: Sealed orders reach you a week after your debrief. The officer's hand: the Order launders blacksteel through the free port at Wake Island, where no village law reaches. Go there. Enter the island's sparring circuit as your cover, and keep your eyes on the water.
Travel to Wake Island, the neutral ground beyond village law.
The circuit master looks you over in a converted fish hall that smells of salt and old blood. Village stamps mean nothing here, they say. The circuit ranks you by wins. Everyone talks to a winner.
Win spars to establish yourself in the Wake Island circuit.

Three wins buys you a bench and a bowl. The fighters talk freely now: crates with violet seams move through the night docks, and the crews that carry them never drink at the circuit. Somebody pays them too well to be seen.
Climb the circuit rankings. The finalists know the island best.

A finalist with burn-scarred hands pulls you aside after your bout. I carried those crates once, they say, flexing fingers that no longer fully close. The manifests go through the harbor office. What is on them is not on any tide chart.
Make your way to the harbor office on the far side of Wake Island.
Recover a discarded tide manifest scrap from the sea-lane caches.
The scrap decodes against the officer's cipher from your Trials days. A shipment moves tonight, two handlers, out along the shallows. Blacksteel does not swim. Stop it before it sinks out of reach.
Intercept the shipment and defeat the two handlers before the cargo disappears.
objectives.drawDescription: Neither side yielded. The contract stands.
objectives.failDescription: They were stronger than the posting suggested. Regroup.

objectives.description: The handlers slipped you in the shallows. Return to the circuit, patch up, and read the tides again.

The cargo sits beached and violet-veined at your feet. Word travels fast on a small island: by morning, the circuit knows exactly what you are, and nobody minds. Wake Island respects a winner with a cause.

The officer arrives on the next tide, in person, and reads everything twice in a rented back room. Then they produce a form you have never seen and sign it without ceremony. My recommendation for the Chunin Exams, they say. When you pass, there is a stronghold at your level waiting. The Order keeps a CHUNIN operation too.
Circuit champion, evidence secured, recommendation signed. Wake Island will remember you. So will the Order.

data.name: Copies, Not Thefts
data.description: Three of the Kage's letters were copied, not stolen. Get inside a private archive, take back the files, and bring home the ledger that names the buyer. How quietly you do it is up to you.
data.successDescription: Congratulations! You've successfully won the battle

objectives.description:
The briefing room is lit by one lantern over the map table. The Commander does not sit.

"Three of the Kage's letters left this village and came back as copies. Copies, not thefts. Someone wanted us blind, not angry.
The paper traces to a private archive that keeps records for anyone who pays."

nextObjectiveId.text: Why is ANBU not handling this openly?

objectives.description:
She sets a marker on the map, well outside the wall.

"That is what you will find out. Bring back what they hold and the ledger that says who paid. Nobody knows you were there.
One detail, since you will be reading their shelves: that archive files by season, not by year. Anyone who asks for a year has never been inside."

nextObjectiveId.text: And if the door is watched?

objectives.description:
The mission clerk has your kit ready before you reach the counter.

"Lockpicks, ink kit, two smoke tags, and a writ that will not survive a careful reader.
Sign here. Not with your real name, obviously."
Cross to the archive district under dark.

The safehouse smells of cold tea. Through the shutter slat you can see the archive door across the alley.

Two guards, one circuit, four minutes apart. There will be a service way in around the back, and a roof line if you would rather be quick than careful.
Work the alley behind the archive and map the ways in.

Three ways in, and the patrol turns in ninety seconds.

The coal chute is filthy, blind and slow. The roof line is quick and completely exposed. The front door would take the writ and a steady face.

nextObjectiveId.text: Take the coal chute. Slow and unseen.
Go over the roof line. Fast and loud.

objectives.description: Crawl the coal chute, one shoulder at a time, and drop into the cellar.

You come out under the stacks with soot in your teeth and nobody the wiser.

Above you the building is quiet in the way that means everyone in it believes they are alone.

The tiles are wet and one of them moves under your foot.

Across the roof a lookout turns, sees you, and does not shout. He reaches for the bell rope instead, which is worse.
Take the lookout down before he reaches the rope.
objectives.drawDescription: Neither side yielded. The contract stands.
objectives.failDescription: They were stronger than the posting suggested. Regroup.

objectives.description:
He does not reach it. But he got a hand to it, and somewhere below a small bell moved once.

One ring is not an alarm. It is a question. Someone in this building is already walking toward the answer.

nextObjectiveId.text: Get inside before they find it.

objectives.description:
The clerk reads the writ twice, which is once more than you wanted.

"Requisition, then. Which index do you need pulled?"

nextObjectiveId.text: The index for the year, all of it.
Whichever one the Kage's office uses.

objectives.description:
He nods, bored, and writes it down. Everyone who works here knows they file by season. Only outsiders ask for a year.

"Third aisle, and do not take the lamp past the ledgers."
He goes back to his tea. You walk into the archive through the front door like a man with business here.

He smiles, and the smile does not reach anything.

"We do not index by year. Never have."
The writ goes in his pocket, not back in your hand, and two men walk you out. By the time you are in the alley again the lamps are lit on the upper floor and the building knows it has a visitor.

nextObjectiveId.text: Go over the roof, then. Nothing quiet left to lose.

objectives.description:
Rows of shelving run back into the dark, every one packed with rolled paper.

Somewhere below, a single lamp is still burning. Seasons, not years. The autumn shelves are the far wall.
Search the seasonal shelves for the transfer ledger.

The ledger is ordinary until the last three pages.

Every transfer in the same neat hand, buyer left, price right. Your village letters are listed twice.
The name beside them is one you have heard in a briefing room, on the other side of the table.

nextObjectiveId.text: Copy the page and get the files.

objectives.description: Work the seal on the file drawer.

Someone has been in the room the whole time.

He steps out from between the shelves without hurrying, which is worse than if he ran. No crest, no colours, nothing to say who pays him. Only the way he stands, which says he has done this before.
objectives.drawDescription: Neither side yielded. The contract stands.
objectives.failDescription: They were stronger than the posting suggested. Regroup.

objectives.description: Take the ledger and the files out the way you came, and cross back over the border before first light.

The Commander reads the page twice, then sets it face down on the map.

"You were not seen. Good.
As for this name, you will forget you read it until I tell you to remember. That is not a request, and it is not for your protection."

data.name: Dusk Workspace (keep out)
data.description: I SAID KEEP OUT WE LEARNING IN HERE

objectives.description: To the world, Dusk is still missing. But you know more than most—you saw him change, saw him fly away into the twilight.  If he left anything behind, it would be here. His shack, simple and weathered, stands waiting. You steel yourself, and push the door open.
The room smells faintly of smoke and ink. Dust coats the shelves, yet everything feels deliberate. Three things stand out among the clutter, each too carefully placed to be forgotten.
The desk is strewn with broken chopsticks and lacquer shavings. Only one piece is whole: two lacquered sticks tied with red ribbon, blossoms that never wilt, their edges smoldering faintly.
A small, corrupted creature snores in the corner. It looks twisted, but strangely at peace.
A worn field guide lies open on the desk. It’s signed “Jaktik,” but the handwriting is unmistakably Dusk’s.
Lifting the Memento reveals a burn-shadow scorched into the wood — blossoms outlined, with one hex seared deeper than the rest.

The guide lies open, margins filled with Jaktik’s notes. One page shows a rough map of Seichi with a single spot circled hard in ink. The entry beside it reads: Redhour Blossom — blooms rarely, but here it opens every sunset without fail. Petals flare crimson, then fade. I lingered too long. Something in me moved with them. The horizon felt alive.

The Hollowfoot dozes softly. Around its neck hangs a circular charm, worn smooth. On the front, etched in block letters: LEFTY. You turn it over — the back is carved with a crude map, a cluster of hexes with one marked clearly. It matches the shape of Seichi’s world map.

objectives.description: Maemi: “This is a founder’s capsule. These were left by the first survivors who climbed from the ruins of Samui and built what would become Akikaze. If our enemies carried this, they are not simply attacking our village. They are attacking our memory.”

data.description: Akikaze Village summons you after disturbances shake its sky-bridges and sacred wind channels. Uncover the Grounded Spiral, survive the aerial assault, and discover what still echoes in the gust.
data.successDescription: You defended Akikaze, restored the source wind channel, and helped the village recover a forgotten part of its history.

objectives.description: Saeji: “Veyra is heading for the source channel. No bridge is safe, and the elevators are locked down. We climb the wind or we lose the village.”

nextObjectiveId.text: Use a glider and ascend through the storm.

objectives.description: You ride an emergency glider through violent updrafts and land hard on the storm-battered temple. Sacred chimes crack beneath the pressure of Veyra’s engine.

nextObjectiveId.text: Face Veyra beside the source channel.

objectives.description: Every alternate route is collapsing. Saeji warns that another delay will let Veyra reverse the source channel completely.

Veyra: “Look at these carvings. Akikaze shows courage and divine wind—but where are the wounded, the old, and those who could not rise? They carved themselves into heroes and scratched us from stone.”

nextObjectiveId.text: You’re right that history was hidden, but this attack must stop.
Akikaze survived. That is all that matters.
Destroying the village will not honor the forgotten.

objectives.description: Veyra: “Pretty words from someone standing in the sky. If Akikaze will not descend to remember us, then I will drag its heavens down.”
Veyra: “Then you have learned nothing. You are not here to heal Akikaze’s wound. You are here to guard its lie.”
Veyra reverses the source channel and surrounds the temple in crushing downward wind.
objectives.drawDescription: The deadlock lasts too long; Akikaze enters emergency lockdown.
objectives.failDescription: The Grounded Spiral overwhelms the defense and escapes with the wind-channel data.
objectives.fleeDescription: Your retreat gives the Grounded Spiral enough time to complete its sabotage.
objectives.successDescription: Veyra falls, but the unstable fragment engine begins to rupture.

objectives.description: The engine screams as two forces tear at the storm: artificial pressure forcing the wind down and the ancient updraft struggling to rise. The wrong answer will destroy everything.

nextObjectiveId.text: Force your chakra into the engine.
Redirect the current and loosen the control ring.

objectives.description: You move with the current instead of against it. The loosened ring gives the trapped updraft a path to rise. The machine ruptures and the source channel roars back to life.

nextObjectiveId.text: Return with the recovered chime fragments.

objectives.description: The village gathers around the damaged carvings and recovered chime fragments. For the first time, Akikaze displays the images of those who could not climb from Samui.

nextObjectiveId.text: Listen to Maemi address the village.

objectives.description: Maemi: “We were born from ascent, but ascent is not innocence. Some could not follow. Some were lost. Some were left. From this day forward, Akikaze will let the wind carry all their names.”
Shion: “From broken bronze, cracked silver, and temple crystal, we will forge a new chime. It will ring for those who climbed, those who could not, and those still searching for the courage to rise.”

nextObjectiveId.text: Speak with Saeji one last time.

objectives.description: Saeji: “You followed the echo when others heard only noise. Akikaze owes you its thanks. Iroha says you broke less than expected, which from her is basically a love poem.”

nextObjectiveId.text: Listen as the new chime rings.

objectives.description: Akikaze’s new memorial chime rings for those who climbed and those left below. The truth finally echoes in the gust.
